q: The support system is very important to all living things such as plants, animals and ____ .
e: The support system is very important to all living things such as plants, animals and humans. Humans is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Plants do not have skeletons like animals but they use their ____ of cells within packing tissue for support.
e: Plants do not have skeletons like animals but they use their turgidity of cells within packing tissue for support. Turgidity is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In humans and other animals, the main body support is provided by the internal skeletal system of ____ .
e: In humans and other animals, the main body support is provided by the internal skeletal system of bones. Bones is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In some animals, the skeleton is ____ as in insects and prawns.
e: In some animals, the skeleton is external as in insects and prawns. External is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The skeleton supports body weight, maintains body shape, protects ____ organs inside the body.
e: The skeleton supports body weight, maintains body shape, protects soft organs inside the body. Soft is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Support in woody plants has specialized tissue to give them support, which has ____ cell wall.
e: Support in woody plants has specialized tissue to give them support, which has cellulose cell wall. Plant cell walls are made of cellulose.

q: The physiological support is a temporary support because it depends on the presence of ____ in the plant cells.
e: The physiological support is a temporary support because it depends on the presence of water in the plant cells. Water is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The structural support is a ____ support.
e: The structural support is a permanent support. Permanent is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Support in non-woody plants depends on the turgidity of their cells such as ____ and collenchyma.
e: Support in non-woody plants depends on the turgidity of their cells such as parenchyma and collenchyma. Parenchyma is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Roots which grow down from the stem or branches into the ground for support are called ____ roots.
e: Roots which grow down from the stem or branches into the ground for support are called prop roots. Prop is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The thick support roots that grow from the stem above the ground are called ____ roots.
e: The thick support roots that grow from the stem above the ground are called buttress roots. Buttress is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The movement of a plant in response to light is known as ____ .
e: The movement of a plant in response to light is known as phototropism. Phototropism is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The movement of a plant part towards the soil in response to earth's gravity is known as ____ .
e: The movement of a plant part towards the soil in response to earth's gravity is known as geotropism. Geotropism is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The movement of the plant towards the water is known as ____ .
e: The movement of the plant towards the water is known as hydrotropism. Hydrotropism is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The movement of plants in response to a chemical stimulus is known as ____ .
e: The movement of plants in response to a chemical stimulus is known as chemotropism. Chemotropism is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The directional movement in plants in response to touch is known as ____ .
e: The directional movement in plants in response to touch is known as thigmotropism. Thigmotropism is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The movement of plant or their parts in response to changes in the external stimulus of temperature is known as ____ .
e: The movement of plant or their parts in response to changes in the external stimulus of temperature is known as thermotropism. Thermotropism is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Nastic movements in plants are not ____ movements.
e: Nastic movements in plants are not directional movements. Directional is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The leaves of ‘touch me not’ fold up immediately when ____ .
e: The leaves of ‘touch me not’ fold up immediately when touched. Touched is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The closing of the lid of insectivorous plant occurs due to the catchment of ____ .
e: The closing of the lid of insectivorous plant occurs due to the catchment of insects. Insects is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The skeletal system in animals is commonly recognized as hydrostatic skeleton, exoskeleton and ____ .
e: The skeletal system in animals is commonly recognized as hydrostatic skeleton, exoskeleton and endoskeleton. Endoskeleton is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Hydrostatic skeletons are found primarily in soft-bodied terrestrial invertebrates such as ____ .
e: Hydrostatic skeletons are found primarily in soft-bodied terrestrial invertebrates such as earthworms. Earthworms is the idea that completes this fact.

q: An exoskeleton is a rigid, hard case that surrounds the body of ____ .
e: An exoskeleton is a rigid, hard case that surrounds the body of arthropods. Arthropods is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Endoskeletons found in vertebrates are rigid internal ____ .
e: Endoskeletons found in vertebrates are rigid internal skeletons. The skeleton supports the body, protects organs, and gives muscles something to pull on.

q: The human skeleton has about ____ bones.
e: The human skeleton has about 206 bones. 206 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The bones of the skeleton provide sites for ____ attachment.
e: The bones of the skeleton provide sites for muscle attachment. The skeleton supports the body, protects organs, and gives muscles something to pull on.

q: The axial skeleton includes the bones found in the ____ and head of the body.
e: The axial skeleton includes the bones found in the trunk and head of the body. Trunk is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The axial skeleton includes the ____ pairs of ribs.
e: The axial skeleton includes the 12 pairs of ribs. Carbon-12 is the mass standard: one-twelfth of that atom is the atomic mass unit.

q: The appendicular skeleton is adapted to allow the body to ____ .
e: The appendicular skeleton is adapted to allow the body to move. Move is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The appendicular skeleton includes the bones in the limbs that extend from the ____ of the body.
e: The appendicular skeleton includes the bones in the limbs that extend from the trunk of the body. Trunk is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Bone tissue consists of a dense and hard organic matrix deposits of ____ in between the bone cells.
e: Bone tissue consists of a dense and hard organic matrix deposits of minerals in between the bone cells. Minerals is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Cartilage is a flexible connective tissue found between the ____ .
e: Cartilage is a flexible connective tissue found between the bones. Bones is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A joint is the place where two ____ meet.
e: A joint is the place where two bones meet. Bones is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Fibrous joints are made of the same dense material that bone is made of and they act like a tough ____ that connects the bones.
e: Fibrous joints are made of the same dense material that bone is made of and they act like a tough glue that connects the bones. Glue is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Cartilaginous joints allow ____ movement.
e: Cartilaginous joints allow partial movement. Partial is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Synovial joints are cushioned with cartilage and held together by a capsule of ____ .
e: Synovial joints are cushioned with cartilage and held together by a capsule of ligaments. Ligaments is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Synovial joints allow a great degree of ____ between bones.
e: Synovial joints allow a great degree of movement between bones. Movement is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The healthy musculoskeletal system allows for normal physical activities such as walking, running, ____ and other activities.
e: The healthy musculoskeletal system allows for normal physical activities such as walking, running, jumping and other activities. Jumping is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Abnormal joints and muscles result in ____ in which damaged ends of bones rub against each other.
e: Abnormal joints and muscles result in osteoarthritis in which damaged ends of bones rub against each other. Osteoarthritis is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Physical activities and exercises are necessary to maintain healthy ____ between bones.
e: Physical activities and exercises are necessary to maintain healthy joints between bones. Joints is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Some movements can cause injuries, leading to joint damage involving ____ and ligaments.
e: Some movements can cause injuries, leading to joint damage involving cartilages and ligaments. Cartilages is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Health of bones, joints and muscles can be supported by healthy ____ .
e: Health of bones, joints and muscles can be supported by healthy food. Food is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Vitamins C, K and A, iron, calcium, phosphorus and magnesium are good for ____ .
e: Vitamins C, K and A, iron, calcium, phosphorus and magnesium are good for joints. Joints is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Proteins play a critical role in muscle and cartilage ____ .
e: Proteins play a critical role in muscle and cartilage repair. Repair is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Reducing body weight by exercising regularly reduces joint pain, improves joint health and keeps ____ strong.
e: Reducing body weight by exercising regularly reduces joint pain, improves joint health and keeps muscle strong. Muscle is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The plants are fixed at a place with their ____ in the ground.
e: The plants are fixed at a place with their roots in the ground. Roots is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Although they cannot move from one place to another by their bodies, they can move with their ____ .
e: Although they cannot move from one place to another by their bodies, they can move with their parts. Parts is the idea that completes this fact.

q: These movements are caused due to response of plants to external stimuli such as light, water, ____ , chemicals, etc.
e: These movements are caused due to response of plants to external stimuli such as light, water, gravity, chemicals, etc. Gravity is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Plants show two types of movements: growth-dependent movements called the ____ movements and non-growth dependent movements called the nastic movements.
e: Plants show two types of movements: growth-dependent movements called the tropic movements and non-growth dependent movements called the nastic movements. Tropic is the idea that completes this fact.

q: If the movement is towards the direction of stimuli, it is known as ____ tropism.
e: If the movement is towards the direction of stimuli, it is known as positive tropism. Positive is the idea that completes this fact.

q: If the movement is away from the stimuli, it is known as ____ tropism.
e: If the movement is away from the stimuli, it is known as negative tropism. Negative is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Tropic movements in plants can be classified into six types: phototropism, geotropism, hydrotropism, ____ , thigmotropism, and thermotropism.
e: Tropic movements in plants can be classified into six types: phototropism, geotropism, hydrotropism, chemotropism, thigmotropism, and thermotropism. Chemotropism is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Plants are very sensitive to light, and the movement of plants in response to light is known as ____ .
e: Plants are very sensitive to light, and the movement of plants in response to light is known as phototropism. Phototropism is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In geotropism, the shoot is negatively geotropic and the root is positively ____ .
e: In geotropism, the shoot is negatively geotropic and the root is positively geotropic. Geotropic is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The movement of the plant towards the water is known as ____ .
e: The movement of the plant towards the water is known as hydrotropism. Hydrotropism is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The movement of plants in response to a chemical stimulus is known as ____ .
e: The movement of plants in response to a chemical stimulus is known as chemotropism. Chemotropism is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The directional movement in plants in response to touch is known as ____ .
e: The directional movement in plants in response to touch is known as thigmotropism. Thigmotropism is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Thermotropism is the movement of plant or their parts in response to changes in the external stimulus of ____ .
e: Thermotropism is the movement of plant or their parts in response to changes in the external stimulus of temperature. Temperature is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Nastic movements in plants are not dependent on the direction of the ____ .
e: Nastic movements in plants are not dependent on the direction of the stimulus. A stimulus is a change in the surroundings that an organism can detect.

q: For example, the leaves of ‘touch me not’ fold up immediately when ____ .
e: For example, the leaves of ‘touch me not’ fold up immediately when touched. Touched is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In another example, the closing of the lid of insectivorous plant occurs due to the catchment of the ____ .
e: In another example, the closing of the lid of insectivorous plant occurs due to the catchment of the insects. Insects is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The ability to move in animals is made possible by the combination of a semi rigid skeletal system with joints that act as ____ .
e: The ability to move in animals is made possible by the combination of a semi rigid skeletal system with joints that act as hinges. Hinges is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Muscular action produces a change in body shape, which places a force on different parts of the ____ environment.
e: Muscular action produces a change in body shape, which places a force on different parts of the outside environment. Outside is the idea that completes this fact.

q: For example, when a horse runs, its feet contact the ground, and the force they exert moves its body ____ .
e: For example, when a horse runs, its feet contact the ground, and the force they exert moves its body forward. Forward is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In a similar way, when a bird takes off into flight, its wings exert force on the ____ .
e: In a similar way, when a bird takes off into flight, its wings exert force on the air. Air is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Locomotion in earthworms involves a fluid-filled central body cavity or coelom encompassed by two sets of muscles in the body wall: circular muscles and ____ muscles.
e: Locomotion in earthworms involves a fluid-filled central body cavity or coelom encompassed by two sets of muscles in the body wall: circular muscles and longitudinal muscles. Longitudinal is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Short and bristle-like structures called ____ are on the underside of a worm’s body.
e: Short and bristle-like structures called setae are on the underside of a worm’s body. Setae is the idea that completes this fact.

q: This locomotion process proceeds as waves of circular-muscle contraction followed by waves of longitudinal muscle contraction which pass ____ .
e: This locomotion process proceeds as waves of circular-muscle contraction followed by waves of longitudinal muscle contraction which pass backward. Backward is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In the anterior end, circular muscles contract and longitudinal muscles relax, causing setae to lose contact with the ____ .
e: In the anterior end, circular muscles contract and longitudinal muscles relax, causing setae to lose contact with the ground. Ground is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Next, the circular muscles contract; the longitudinal muscles relax, causing the anterior of the body to swell and setae to anchor the ____ .
e: Next, the circular muscles contract; the longitudinal muscles relax, causing the anterior of the body to swell and setae to anchor the ground. Ground is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The body region behind the anterior end is pulled forward, and setae prevent slipping ____ of the front end.
e: The body region behind the anterior end is pulled forward, and setae prevent slipping backward of the front end. Backward is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Jumping in grasshoppers involves the flexor and ____ muscles attached to the internal surface of the exoskeleton.
e: Jumping in grasshoppers involves the flexor and extensor muscles attached to the internal surface of the exoskeleton. Extensor is the idea that completes this fact.

q: When the flexor muscle contracts, the leg jerks backwards, propelling the grasshopper ____ .
e: When the flexor muscle contracts, the leg jerks backwards, propelling the grasshopper forward. Forward is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The movement of raising and lowering wings in flight is achieved by the alternate contraction of extensor muscles and ____ muscles.
e: The movement of raising and lowering wings in flight is achieved by the alternate contraction of extensor muscles and flexor muscles. Flexor is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Fish have a streamlined body shape for swimming in water to reduce ____ .
e: Fish have a streamlined body shape for swimming in water to reduce friction. Friction is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Fish move forward as a result of the contraction and relaxation of muscles called ____ on either side of the body.
e: Fish move forward as a result of the contraction and relaxation of muscles called myotomes on either side of the body. Myotomes is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Pectoral fins are used to steer the fish, while pelvic fins are used to balance the fish and prevent it from ____ .
e: Pectoral fins are used to steer the fish, while pelvic fins are used to balance the fish and prevent it from diving. Diving is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The frog’s powerful hind legs are adapted for both swimming and ____ .
e: The frog’s powerful hind legs are adapted for both swimming and leaping. Leaping is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The strong extensor muscles of the thigh contract, extending the limb and thrusting the foot against the ground or against the ____ .
e: The strong extensor muscles of the thigh contract, extending the limb and thrusting the foot against the ground or against the water. Water is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Most birds have approximately ____ different muscles, mainly controlling the wings, skin, and legs.
e: Most birds have approximately 175 different muscles, mainly controlling the wings, skin, and legs. 175 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: During flight, a bird moves its wings in a pattern of upstrokes and ____ .
e: During flight, a bird moves its wings in a pattern of upstrokes and downstrokes. Downstrokes is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The antagonistic muscle pair of pectoral and supracoracoideus forms the major flight muscles, allowing for effective wing ____ .
e: The antagonistic muscle pair of pectoral and supracoracoideus forms the major flight muscles, allowing for effective wing movement. Movement is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In humans, there are about ____ skeletal muscles that function in antagonistic pairs for locomotion and movement.
e: In humans, there are about 650 skeletal muscles that function in antagonistic pairs for locomotion and movement. 650 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: One prominent example pair of muscles is biceps brachii and triceps brachii in the upper arm, where contraction of biceps brachii ____ the forearm towards the upper arm.
e: One prominent example pair of muscles is biceps brachii and triceps brachii in the upper arm, where contraction of biceps brachii flexes the forearm towards the upper arm. Flexes is the idea that completes this fact.

q: When the triceps brachii is relaxed, flexion happens at the hinge joint at the ____ .
e: When the triceps brachii is relaxed, flexion happens at the hinge joint at the elbow. Elbow is the idea that completes this fact.

q: But when the biceps relaxes and the triceps contracts, the forearm is pulled away from the ____ .
e: But when the biceps relaxes and the triceps contracts, the forearm is pulled away from the upper arm. Upper arm is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Another example pair of muscles is the hamstring and quadriceps muscles in the thigh of the legs, where contraction of the hamstring and relaxing of the quadriceps flex the leg at the ____ .
e: Another example pair of muscles is the hamstring and quadriceps muscles in the thigh of the legs, where contraction of the hamstring and relaxing of the quadriceps flex the leg at the knee. Knee is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Next, the leg is extended at the knee by contraction of the quadriceps and relaxing of the hamstring muscles, showing the action of ____ pairs.
e: Next, the leg is extended at the knee by contraction of the quadriceps and relaxing of the hamstring muscles, showing the action of antagonistic pairs. Antagonistic is the idea that completes this fact.
